title: Peaches and Inkpot's Sparkle Cake Mystery
markdown:
Peaches was a parrot with feathers the colour of a juicy sunset and a squawk that could make a grumpy badger do a cartwheel. She did not care about boring old seeds. She dreamt of huge pirate feasts: tables piled high with gigantic mangoes, rivers of fizzy raspberry juice, and pies so big they would need their own tiny island. “A feast fit for a captain,” she would announce, usually to a very confused starfish.

One blustery afternoon the wind whistled a happy tune, and Peaches rummaged in a dusty old sea chest that looked as if it had sailed to the moon and back. Her curious beak nudged a recipe card: crinkly, smelling of salty sea spray and cinnamon, for Captain Crunchy’s Cove Cake. There was a mystery. A missing ingredient: Sparkle-Shell Spice.

“Sparkle-Shell Spice?” Peaches muttered, tilting her head so far it almost fell off. “What on earth is that?” The card had a drawing of a cove shaped like a giant smile, with a bold X marking Secret Sandy Oven. A secret. Peaches did a little hop-skip on her perch.

A tiny click-clack-click echoed from the sand. Inkpot the crab, shell swirled with ocean blues and greens, tap-danced on the shore. He was not a squawker. He was a scuttler, a planner, and he had a nose for treasure.

“Squawk-a-doo, Inkpot. I found a pirate recipe, but it needs Sparkle-Shell Spice.”

Inkpot stopped his tap-dancing and wiggled his antennae. “Sparkle-Shell Spice,” he clicked, voice like smooth pebbles. “I know a place. Where the shells sparkle.”

Peaches’s feathers fluffed. “Then we’re going. Right now. To the Secret Sandy Oven.”

So Peaches, clutching the recipe card, and Inkpot, perched on a folded corner like a tiny captain, set off in a rather leaky coconut shell Inkpot had borrowed for essential maritime travel. As they floated along, a gigantic shadow fell over them. With a mighty thump a huge pelican landed right beside their coconut boat.

This was Branwen the Boisterous. Branwen was not exactly friendly. She had a beak like a cavernous bucket and a laugh that sounded like a rusty door hinge screaming for oil.

“Ooh, what’s this?” she boomed, beady eyes glinting. “A map. Gimme that. I’m the best pirate.” She lunged, beak opening wider than a hungry hippo’s yawn.

“Yikes,” squawked Peaches, bright feathers fluffed. The beak snapped shut with a whoosh, a gust of fishy air stinging her nostrils as the dark shadow blotted out the sun. Inkpot, with a speed that defied his size, clicked, “Swamped.” Peaches flapped with all her might, a whirlwind of orange and yellow. The coconut wobbled. They shot forward, leaving Branwen flapping, sputtering, and kicking up a huge spray. “Too close,” Peaches panted, heart doing a drum solo against her ribs. Branwen spluttered like a leaky faucet — not exactly the fearsome pirate she imagined herself to be.

They reached a dense misty mangrove swamp. The air, thick and warm, clung to Peaches’s feathers like a damp blanket. Distant squawks of unseen birds pierced the muffled quiet. Gnarled roots coiled like sleeping pythons.

“Which way now, Inkpot?”

Inkpot scuttled back and forth. “I don’t know,” he clicked, voice uncharacteristically small. Inkpot not knowing? That was like a cloud not knowing how to rain. Peaches missed her safe sunny perch.

Then she remembered something. Tucked away on the recipe card, almost invisible, was a tiny note: Follow the tinkles when the fog is thickest.

“Tinkles. Inkpot, listen. Do you hear that?”

Faintly, a delicate sound, like miniature bells dancing. “Tinkles,” Inkpot echoed, antennae perking up.

The tinkles led them deeper, growing louder. They emerged into a small sun-dappled clearing. In the centre was a cave, guarded by monkeys. Chatter, chatter, chatter.

“Riddles. Riddles. Answer our riddles, or no pass through.”

Peaches gulped. Riddles? She was better at squawking. She looked at Inkpot, little claws planted firmly, and puffed out her chest. The monkeys asked, and Peaches, to her surprise, got them all right: one about the sky, one about the sea, and one about a very grumpy starfish. The monkeys giggled. Then, with a blur of brown fur, the water skin poofed upwards, a cascade of chattering laughter as the mischief in the monkeys’ eyes vanished into the leaves.

“Hey,” squawked Peaches.

“Oh, bother,” clicked Inkpot, voice flatter than a pancake.

After a long thirsty journey, guided only by the fading tinkles and their determination, they arrived at a hidden cove. A soft sandy beach. Gentle waves. A cave that looked exactly like the one on the map. This must be the Secret Sandy Oven. Peaches flew inside, Inkpot scuttling behind. It was warm and dry, a perfect place for baking, though it looked like just a cave. And where was the oven? And the Sparkle-Shell Spice? All they saw were dusty rocks and empty shells.

Peaches looked at the shells, then at the recipe card. A little spark began to glow. “What if the spice is in the shells?”

Inkpot, who had been tapping at them, suddenly clicked with excitement. “Peaches. The shells. They’re not just shells.” He nudged one toward sunlight. It shimmered with tiny rainbow colours, like captured stars. “It’s the Sparkle-Shell Spice.”

Peaches’s heart soared. “It’s not an ingredient you find. It’s one you make.”

They gathered more shells, and Inkpot, with surprisingly strong little claws, began grinding them against the sandy floor. A fine shimmering powder rose, swirling like fairy dust. It smelled of fresh sea air and something wonderfully sweet. They mixed this sparkling powder with wild berries Peaches had found and some tender seaweed Inkpot discovered. They placed their mixture into a hollowed-out rock — their very own Secret Sandy Oven.

The result was not quite a cake, but a delightful sweet-tart mash, bursting with flavours so wonderful their taste buds did a little happy dance. It was the most delicious thing they had ever tasted.

“See?” clicked Inkpot, antennae wiggling. “It wasn’t just the spice. It was the whole adventure. And you. You were super clever, Peaches.”

Peaches puffed out her chest, a happy squawk escaping her. “And you were super brave, Inkpot. We did it.”

They shared their Sparkle-Shell feast just like legendary pirates, two small cooks in a smiling cove, the coconut boat waiting, and Branwen somewhere far behind them still practising her pirate laugh on an empty stretch of sea.
